Joseph was brought down to Egypt.

Brought down.
The descent continues.
Pit, caravan, Egypt, Potiphar's house.
Each step lower.

Sold.
Purchased.
Owned.
The Lord was with Joseph.
the Lord was with Joseph.

after the purchase, the Lord was with him.
Not a dream.
Not a voice.
Not an angel.
Just: the Lord was with him.

Successful.

The slave prospers.
Not because he is free.
Not because he is home.

Through a pagan.

and inside the going-down, he rises.
Still a slave.
Still in Egypt.
Still far from home.

in the house and in the field.

For Joseph's sake.

The Cup of integrity,
held by a man who serves faithfully in a house that is not his home.

handsome in form and appearance.

the desire of those who see.

his master's wife set her eyes on Joseph and said:

He refused.

Judah took.

my master does not know what is with me in the house,

How can I sin against God?
Joseph names God.
In an Egyptian house.
To an Egyptian woman.
The slave who was sold by his brothers, carried by Ishmaelites,
bought by an Egyptian,
names the God of his fathers as the reason he will not take.
The recognition that has been deception for three chapters is now integrity.
Joseph recognizes God where no one else does.

Every person in Genesis who had power took what they wanted.
Joseph has power, he refuses.
The Cup of integrity:
the first person in Genesis who could take and doesn't.

Day after day.

Not a single moment.

Every morning, the same voice.

She grabs.
He runs.
The garment, is seized.

He ran.
He did not argue.
He did not negotiate.
He did not explain.
He left the garment and ran.
Flight as integrity.
Not cowardice, refusal.

The man who will not take what is offered also will not stay to be taken.

He came in to me to lie with me.
